title: Amazon S3 to Amazon SQS to AWS Lambda
description: Create a Lambda function that resizes images uploaded to S3 via SQS.

introBox.headline: How it works
text: The SAM template deploys a Lambda function, an SQS queue, 2 S3 buckets and the IAM resources required to run the application.

The source bucket sends an ObjectCreated event to the SQS queue for each uploaded .jpg file. The queue triggers the Lambda function, which reports failed messages so one bad image doesn't retry the whole batch.
The function resizes the image with sharp and saves it in the destination bucket. Both buckets block public access, so the resized images stay private.

bullets.text: Building resilient serverless patterns by combining messaging services

testing.headline: Testing
text: 1. Upload a .jpg image to the source bucket. Replace {SourceBucketName} with the name from the stack outputs.
2. Check that the resized image is in the destination bucket.
3. Check that the image is private. A request without credentials returns 403 Forbidden.

cleanup.headline: Cleanup
text: 1. Empty both buckets, then delete the stack: sam delete --stack-name STACK_NAME.
2. Confirm the stack has been deleted: aws cloudformation list-stacks --query "StackSummaries[?contains(StackName,'STACK_NAME')].StackStatus"
